question: Gemini 4's RYS idea 2: does the second traversal of a repeated block amplify the first's writes (e509's chord sparing) or erase and recompute them (LOOPED.md, e648b's read repulsion), and does the answer split by family as e651's GELU-only read-write anti-alignment predicts?
design: the three least and three most damaging blocks of two or more layers (e656); per band block and sampled position: second-vs-first MLP output cosine, share of the first's eight largest writes gone from the second's eight, sign flips among them, activation correlation; band increment cosine and 16-word ledger Jaccard.
smoke: SmolLM2-135M: least damaging 13-17: band increment cosine +0.667, MLP output cosine +0.691, top-8 erased 0.55, sign flips 0.04, activation correlation +0.727; most damaging 0-2: +0.597, +0.332, 0.93, 0.37, +0.065.

P1.text: on the least damaging blocks the second traversal's band increment points along the first's (mean cosine above 0.3)

P2.text: half or more of the first traversal's eight largest MLP writes per token are gone from the second's eight largest

P3.text: the second-to-first MLP output cosine is lower in Pythia-410m (GELU, read repulsion) than in both gated models

P4.text: the least damaging blocks show a higher second-to-first MLP output cosine than the most damaging ones

status: fixed before the full runs; smokes on SmolLM2-135M (a sixth of the blocks; plumbing, seen before these were fixed and reflected in the guesses)
